title: 1Password vs Auth0: Credential Management or Application Identity?
description: 1Password and Auth0 address different identity problems. 1Password helps people and teams manage credentials; Auth0 provides identity capabilities that developers integrate into applications. This guide explains when each is relevant, where they can coexist, and what to verify before selecting either.

features.name: Primary job
features.tool1: Manage passwords and other credentials for people and teams
features.tool1Detail: Evaluate credential storage, secure sharing, team administration, recovery, and access policies.
features.tool2: Provide application authentication and identity flows
features.tool2Detail: Evaluate sign-in requirements, identity integrations, authorization needs, and developer implementation effort.

features.name: Main user
features.tool1Detail: Map the plan and controls to the people who need access to shared credentials.
features.tool2Detail: Map identity requirements to application users, supported flows, and operational ownership.

features.name: Decision criteria
features.tool1Detail: Check recovery options, permission boundaries, administrative controls, and supported devices.
features.tool2Detail: Check required protocols, integration patterns, user volume, security requirements, and support terms.

features.name: Relationship
features.tool1Detail: A credential manager does not replace the identity layer implemented by an application.
features.tool2Detail: An application identity platform does not replace a team's need to store and share internal credentials.

verdict: These products are not direct substitutes, so a single winner would be misleading. Evaluate 1Password if the problem is how people store, share, and govern credentials. Evaluate Auth0 if the problem is how an application authenticates users and manages identity flows. Some teams may need both. Confirm current capabilities, security controls, integrations, support, and pricing with each vendor before committing.

faqs.question: Which is better, 1Password or Auth0?
faqs.answer: Neither is a universal winner because they solve different problems. 1Password focuses on credential management for people and teams; Auth0 helps developers implement identity and authentication in applications. Start with the requirement you need to meet.

faqs.question: Can 1Password replace Auth0?
faqs.answer: No. A credential manager is not an application identity service. If your product needs user sign-in, evaluate an identity platform such as Auth0; if your staff need secure credential storage and sharing, evaluate a password manager.

faqs.question: Can a team use 1Password and Auth0 together?
faqs.answer: Yes, they can serve separate roles. A team may use 1Password for workforce credentials and Auth0 for application identity. Define which system owns each credential or identity workflow, and review permissions and recovery procedures.

faqs.question: How should I compare their costs?
faqs.answer: Do not compare headline prices without matching the scope. Estimate 1Password costs for the users and administrative controls you need. For Auth0, verify the current plan, user or usage assumptions, required features, and support terms for your application. Use current vendor pricing rather than an unverified figure.

faqs.question: What should I verify before choosing?
faqs.answer: For 1Password, check credential sharing, access controls, recovery, administration, and the devices your team uses. For Auth0, check supported identity flows, integrations, authorization needs, implementation effort, security requirements, and operational support. Test the relevant workflows before making a decision.
